title: Linguine al Limone
subtitle: A bright, creamy Italian pasta with lemon and Parmesan
excerpt: This Southern Italian pasta needs very few ingredients and is on the table in 20 minutes. The sauce is just butter, cream, lemon, and Parmesan, loosened with a little pasta water.
sourceNotes: Amalfi Coast and Southern Italian tradition; lemon pasta is closely associated with Campania and Sorrento.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: This dish does not hold well. Make and serve immediately.

content.text: Linguine al limone is one of the simplest pasta dishes in the Italian canon. The sauce emulsifies butter, cream, lemon zest, and starchy pasta water into something silky and light. Move quickly once the pasta drains as the sauce clings best when everything is hot.

items.prepNote: zest of both, juice of one
finely grated, plus more to serve

content.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add salt generously. Cook the linguine for 1 minute less than the packet time. Reserve a large mugful of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, set a wide frying pan over low heat. Add the double cream and lemon zest. Warm gently for 2 minutes. Do not let it boil.
Add the cold butter cubes to the cream, a few at a time, stirring constantly until each piece melts and the sauce looks glossy.
Add the lemon juice and the olive oil. Stir. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen the sauce.
Drain the linguine and add it directly to the sauce pan. Toss vigorously over low heat for one minute, adding more pasta water a little at a time until the sauce coats every strand.
Remove from the heat. Add the grated Parmesan and black pepper. Toss again. Taste for salt and lemon.
Serve in warmed bowls with extra Parmesan grated over. Eat immediately.

items.symptom: The sauce has separated and looks greasy.
items.cause: The heat was too high when the butter went in, or the pasta was not added quickly enough.
items.fix: Keep the heat low throughout. A splash of pasta water and vigorous tossing off the heat usually brings it back together.

items.symptom: The pasta clumps together and the sauce does not cling.
items.cause: The pasta sat in the colander and dried out before joining the sauce.
items.fix: Add the pasta straight from the boiling water to the sauce. Reserve plenty of pasta water and work quickly.

items.symptom: The dish tastes flat and lacks brightness.
items.cause: The lemon flavour was lost during cooking, or not enough zest was used.
items.fix: Add a little fresh lemon juice just before serving, not during cooking. Zest from both lemons is not optional.
